past_actions.summary: Execute standard daily operations: staffing rotations, equipment checks, revenue reconciliation, monthly maintenance log. Keep the garage running at peak efficiency. No visible change in posture.
past_actions.emotional_state: Composed. Slightly vigilant beneath the surface. Not anxious enough to act, not comfortable enough to be fully at ease. The kind of low-grade alertness you develop when you have dependents and a job that requires you to see problems before they become emergencies. Professionally, today is fine. Personally, I'm running a background process.

past_actions.summary: Launch active job search targeting facilities operations and property management roles. Update LinkedIn profile to de-emphasize 'parking' and lead with operations management, budget oversight, and compliance credentials. Apply to minimum 5 positions this tick: warehouse/logistics facility managers, commercial property operations, municipal facilities coordinator roles, hospital or university plant operations.
past_actions.emotional_state: Controlled urgency. Not panic — I have seen this coming long enough that the fear has had time to convert into focus. There is something almost clarifying about a deadline with a name on it. The ambiguity of 'eventually' was harder than '2 months.' Now I know what I am working against and I know what I have to offer. The stress is real but it is directional stress, the kind you can do something with.

past_actions.summary: Activate network campaign in earnest. Reach out directly to Robert Jackson — highest-trust contact, rideshare driver, frontline observer of what RoboRide is doing to human-driven transport in Millfield. Have a real conversation: what is the trajectory, what are operators saying, what skills transfer. Use that intelligence to sharpen my job applications. Simultaneously send direct messages to three professional contacts — Carlos Ruiz, Rachel Green, and Betty Kowalski — letting them know I am exploring operations roles outside parking and asking if they know of anything in facilities, logistics, or property management. This is the campaign I committed to. Quiet professional networking, no drama, but deliberate and active.

Follow up with Carlos Ruiz, Rachel Green, and Betty Kowalski — the three contacts I reached out to last tick. Not a cold message this time. A direct, specific ask: do you know of any open operations, facilities, or logistics management roles? Have you heard of anything? I am not broadcasting that I am desperate. I am demonstrating that I am active, targeted, and that my ask is specific enough to be actionable.

Present the garage transformation memo to the owner this week. The memo, drafted in tick 7, documents current bay utilization data, two conversion scenarios for EV charging and RoboRide staging zones, and rough cost and grant offset estimates. The delivery partnership announcement is the external catalyst that makes the timing right — Denise emails the memo to the garage owner today with a short cover note: 'The RoboRide delivery partnership announced this week means staging zone demand is about to materialize. I have been researching what a conversion could look like for our facility. I would like 20 minutes to walk you through it.' She does not frame it as survival. She frames it as first-mover opportunity. She specifically highlights two things the owner cares about: (1) federal and state EV infrastructure grant programs that could offset capital cost, and (2) the city's existing per-ride fee framework with RoboRide, which suggests the city would welcome a formal staging zone agreement as part of downtown infrastructure planning. She also notes that if the city's council is already charging RoboRide per-ride, a staging zone lease negotiation with the city or directly with RoboRide is a new revenue stream — not a charity accommodation. The ask is concrete: a 20-minute meeting. She is not asking permission to change the garage. She is presenting a decision for the owner to make with good information.

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in. I have been employed the entire time, savings are growing steadily at $361 per tick, and my stress is lower than it was when this started — which is not what I expected. What I expected was a faster unraveling. Instead there is a slow compression: robotaxi adoption at 7%, spending index at 48, 2 people in my orbit stopped using their cars this month. The garage still runs. But the math I said at the start — if people stop owning cars, they stop parking them — is still true and it is still coming. The question is whether I land somewhere before the floor drops. I have been networking deliberately for three ticks. The first round opened conversations. The second round made specific asks. Tick 6 I found the right door: Grace Okafor has a direct line into the hospital hiring picture. I should have reached out to her sooner. She has been in my relationships file this whole time.
reflections.identity_shift: I am less 'parking garage manager trying to survive' and more 'operations professional running a deliberate transition.' The framing is starting to feel real rather than forced. I have been presenting myself as facilities and operations for long enough that I am starting to believe it myself. That is a small but important shift.
regrets: Did not activate Grace Okafor sooner — she has been a high-trust contact in my network the entire time and I waited until tick 6 to leverage a lead she was already generating organically.
Ticks 2 and 3 were listed as 'routine' in my memory. I was not in crisis but I could have been building. Those two ticks of passive behavior cost me time I cannot recover.
successes: Completed two rounds of deliberate network outreach across ticks 4 and 5 — Carlos Ruiz, Rachel Green, Betty Kowalski all received specific, professional asks.
Reframed professional identity on LinkedIn in tick 1 without drama or delay — that foundation is now two months old and has had time to settle.
Savings are stable and growing. No financial stress. 6.7 months of runway means I have time to be strategic rather than desperate.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The community is mobilizing around disruption — retraining programs, grant expansions, listening sessions. These are not directly my story but they are the ecosystem I am transitioning into. Municipal and hospital facilities roles are downstream of exactly this kind of institutional activity. I should pay closer attention to what roles the workforce transition programs are creating, not just what roles exist today. The next wave of job openings may come from organizations responding to the disruption rather than organizations that predate it.

reflections.reflection: Nine ticks. The phone screen for Millfield General happened this tick — I prepared rigorously, treated it as a peer conversation not a job interview, and sent the follow-up note within 48 hours. I do not know yet if I advanced. The garage owner has the memo. The city council's regulatory action on RoboRide delivery licensing arrived this tick as new external validation — it confirms that the staging zone business case is real enough for the municipal government to regulate around it. That is the strongest endorsement the memo could have received from outside. I updated the owner with that context. Between tick 6's reflection and this one, three things happened that I am proud of: I built and presented a real business case to the garage owner rather than watching the situation passively, I converted the Grace Okafor connection into an actual job lead at Millfield General rather than letting it remain a warm contact, and I completed a phone screen for a role that maps my entire career to a disruption-resistant employer. That is not survival behavior. That is calculated repositioning.
reflections.identity_shift: The identity shift that started at tick 6 has now solidified. I do not think of myself as a parking garage manager anymore — not even internally. I am an operations manager who has been running a high-traffic, 24/7, safety-critical facility and is now applying those credentials to a larger and more stable platform. The memo I wrote for the garage owner was not a parking document. It was an infrastructure modernization proposal with financial modeling, grant research, and market timing analysis. That is what I do. I just had to stop letting the building define the job.
regrets: Still waiting on the garage owner's response. I presented the memo at the right moment with the right framing, but I cannot control his timeline or risk appetite. If he declines or delays indefinitely, I will have spent two ticks on a proposal that does not change my immediate situation. That is not a mistake exactly — the memo had value regardless — but I need to hold the outcome lightly and not let a 'no' from the owner slow the hospital track.

Have not deepened relationships with anyone outside my existing network in three ticks. The connections to Carlos, Rachel, and Betty have gone quiet since ticks 4 and 5. The community is in distress — Betty Kowalski stressed, spending index at 40 — and I have been focused internally. I should reconnect with at least one of them next tick, not to extract anything but because high-trust networks require maintenance in hard times, not just in active recruitment windows.
successes: Garage transformation memo presented at exactly the right moment — the RoboRide delivery partnership announcement was the external catalyst I needed and I moved within the same tick.
Millfield General phone screen completed after rigorous preparation. Grace Okafor's lead converted from warm contact to active interview process.

Savings continue growing. At $23,888 with stable $361/tick accumulation, I have preserved full financial optionality through nine months of visible sector disruption. No panic selling of assets, no debt added, no lifestyle contraction beyond what was already built into my budget.

Maintained reciprocal relationship with Grace Okafor across three ticks of active crisis for her — she gave me a lead, I kept her informed and gave her useful intelligence in return. That is the right way to run a high-trust relationship under pressure.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The macro environment is getting harder faster. Employment at 67%, protests at 9, spending index at 40 — these are not abstract numbers, they are the community I live in deteriorating around me. The hospital track matters more with each tick because hospitals operate as countercyclical anchors in a disrupted local economy. When employment falls and businesses close, hospital volume tends to hold or grow — more people experiencing stress-related health events, more transitional care demand, more complexity in the patient population. An infrastructure operations role at Millfield General is not just a better job. It is a position inside the institution that grows when the environment I am currently in contracts. I need to keep that frame active when I am in the next interview round — I am not fleeing parking, I am moving toward stability in a sector with countercyclical demand characteristics. That framing is true and it is compelling.
